summary.short: CFPB final rule under CFPA section 1033 requires banks, credit unions and other financial data providers to make covered consumer financial data available, without fees, to consumers and authorized third parties. Third parties must limit collection and use of that data. Compliance is phased in from 2026 to 2030.
summary.long: The CFPB final rule, effective January 17, 2025, implements CFPA section 1033 by requiring data providers to make covered consumer financial data available to consumers and authorized third parties in electronic form. Covered data concerns Regulation E accounts, Regulation Z credit cards and payment facilitation products; depository institutions at or below the $850 million SBA size standard are excluded, while nondepository providers are covered. Providers must use standardized, machine-readable formats, meet minimum response rates, avoid credential-based screen scraping, and charge no access fees. Third parties must obtain express informed consent, certify limits on collection, use and retention, limit collection duration to one year, provide revocation, and retain records for at least three years. Data aggregators may perform authorization for third parties. CFPB-recognized consensus standards serve as indicia of compliance. Part 1001 treats financial data processing as a financial product or service under the CFPA. Compliance dates are tiered from April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030 by asset size or receipts.

notes: Part 1 of 7 covers the front matter and the preamble through the discussion of 12 CFR 1033.111 and 1033.121. The regulatory text of 12 CFR 1033 and 1001.2 appears in later parts, so relations and entities here reflect only what this part states. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry match was verified. Internal inconsistency: the preamble cites EFTA as 15 U.S.C. 1691 et seq. but the anti-waiver provision as 15 U.S.C. 1693l. Front matter gives an effective date of January 17, 2025 and staggered data-provider compliance dates (April 1, 2026 to April 1, 2030); these events are not coded in this part. Part 2 of 7 is Federal Register preamble: discussion and responses to comments on consensus standards, definitions (consumer, consumer interface, data aggregator, depository institution, developer interface, third party), Subpart B (current data, covered data, exceptions) and Subpart C (consumer and developer interfaces, machine-readable files, fees, standardized format). Operative text is quoted only as context; no obligations, thresholds, events, definitions or enforcement are coded from this part, which belong to the part containing the regulatory text. target_instrument_id is empty throughout because no registry IDs for the CFPA, Regulations E, Z or DD, or the other cited instruments were supplied.
